title: Flat base change of higher quasi-coherent direct images on algebraic spaces
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y'\to Y$ be morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Suppose that $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: inverse images of quasi-compact spaces are quasi-compact and its diagonal is quasi-compact. Suppose $g$ is flat, meaning flat on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Form $X'=X\times_YY'$ with projections $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $M$ be quasi-coherent on $X$ [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Use tensor pullback and direct image on the small etale ringed sites [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], and higher direct images computed by injective resolutions in all module sheaves [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For every $q\geq0$ the canonical flat base-change map is a natural isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{Y'}$-modules
$$\beta^q_{g,M}:g^*R^qf_*M\xrightarrow{\sim}R^qf'_* (g')^*M.$$
The map is the cohomology map of derived exchange in the module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with the flat pullbacks identified with their ordinary exact tensor pullbacks; derived exchange is adjoint to pullback of the direct-image counit. For a second flat morphism $k:Y''\to Y'$, these maps compose to $\beta^q_{gk,M}$ under the canonical pullback-composition identifications. If $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $Y'=\operatorname{Spec}B$, the corresponding map on cohomology is the canonical isomorphism
$$H^q(X,M)\otimes_RB\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(X', (g')^*M),$$
whose value on $a\otimes1$ is the usual cohomological pullback of $a$. There is no properness, Noetherian, finite-type, coherence or flatness assumption on $f$ beyond the stated quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness.

source.place: Tag 073K (lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology), clauses (1) and (2); spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 073C (lemma-flat-morphism-sites); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0E47 (remark-compose-base-change-horizontal) for successive base changes.

proof.text: Write $h=g'$. Flatness is stable under base change, so $h$ is flat. The geometric/ringed flatness comparison and the definition of flat ringed morphism make $g^*$ and $h^*$ exact: inverse image is exact and scalar extension by the flat structural algebra is exact. Hence their derived pullbacks are their termwise exact pullbacks: for an exact functor the termwise functor on complexes is a total left derived functor, so by uniqueness of derived functors $Lg^*$ and $Lh^*$ are identified with termwise $g^*$ and $h^*$. On the small ringed-site models form the derived adjunction mate $\beta_{M[0]}$ of the pullback square. By exact-functor cohomology its degree-$q$ map has source $g^*R^qf_*M$ and target $R^qf'_*h^*M$. This constructs precisely the map in the statement; it does not yet assert invertibility.

source.place: Tag 073K, proof first paragraph; Tag 073C; sites-cohomology Tags 0736 and 07A7

proof.text: We first prove the affine-base cohomology assertion. Set $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $Y'=\operatorname{Spec}B$, and $N=h^*M$. The ring map $A\to B$ is flat by the affine criterion. The space $X$ is quasi-compact since $f$ is quasi-compact and the base is affine; it is quasi-separated by the quasi-separated-source lemma, viewing all spaces over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ through the base-change-of-ground-scheme equivalence. The map $h$ is affine: it is a base change of the map between affine schemes $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. Also $N$ is quasi-coherent. Affine cohomology comparison therefore gives a canonical isomorphism $H^q(X,h_*N)\to H^q(X',N)$. No separatedness of $X$ is used.

Let $\underline A,\underline B$ denote the constant ring sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, and put $T(P)=M\otimes_{\underline A}\underline P$ for an $A$-module $P$. For any presentation $A^{(J)}\to A^{(I)}\to P\to0$, the constant-sheaf functor (sheafification, a left adjoint, of the pointwise constant presheaf) and $M\otimes_{\underline A}-$ both preserve colimits, so the presentation gives $T(P)=\operatorname{coker}(M^{(J)}\to M^{(I)})$. The quasi-coherent kernels/colimits statement makes it quasi-coherent. The affine-chart calculus computes this cokernel and the two sums on $U$, giving $T(P)(U)=M(U)\otimes_AP$, with the specified tensor generators. Thus no equality between arbitrary presheaf tensor sections and sheaf tensor sections is presumed. There is a canonical map $\rho:T(B)\to h_*N$, sending a local tensor $m\otimes b$ to $b\,\eta_h(m)$. It is an isomorphism, as follows on each affine etale chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}C\to X$. The pullback chart $U_B=\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_AB)$ is affine; the Zariski/etale quasi-coherent equivalence and its pullback comparison identify the restriction of $N$ to $U_B$ with the etale module of the Zariski pullback of the module associated to $M(U)$, and the quasi-coherent affine pullback formula then identifies $N(U_B)$ with $M(U)\otimes_C(C\otimes_AB)=M(U)\otimes_AB$, and the direct-image chart projections identify $(h_*N)(U)$ with $N(U_B)$. The affine-chart tensor formula gives the same sections for $T(B)$: locally its tensor is sheafified sectionwise tensor, and scalar extension from the constant $A$-module $B$ gives the associated $C$-module $M(U)\otimes_AB$. Both maps send $m\otimes b$ to $b\eta_h(m)$. They commute with chart restrictions and scalar actions, so $\rho$ is an isomorphism of module sheaves, not just of abstract groups.

source.place: Tag 073K, displayed calculation of g-prime pushforward on affine etale charts

proof.text: For any $P$, the bilinear pairing $(m,p)\mapsto m\otimes p$ defines an $A$-linear natural map $\alpha_P^q:H^q(X,M)\otimes_AP\to H^q(X,T(P))$: its value on $a\otimes p$ is $H^q(m\mapsto m\otimes p)(a)$. The balancing identity follows from the tensor relation, and additivity from additivity of cohomology. For $P=A^r$ this is an isomorphism. Indeed $T(A^r)=M^r$ with its specified inclusions and projections. A finite direct sum of injective resolutions of $M$ is an injective resolution of $M^r$: exactness is componentwise and a finite sum of injectives is injective since its Hom functor is the finite product of the exact Hom functors. Applying sections and taking kernels modulo images gives $H^q(X,M^r)=H^q(X,M)^r$, and the maps of the summands are the specified inclusions. For a matrix between finite free modules the induced map on these groups is the same matrix, so these isomorphisms are natural for every transition map between finite free modules, independently of bases.

source.place: Tag 073K, fourth equality in the final displayed calculation (finite free modules)

proof.text:
By Lazard's theorem take a small directed system of finite free $A$-modules $P_i$ with colimit $B$. Sheaf tensor commutes with colimits, as do constant sheaves by their sheafification adjunction; hence $\varinjlim_iT(P_i)=T(B)$. Colimits of module sheaves have the corresponding underlying abelian colimits. Since $X$ is qcqs, its abelian cohomology commutes with this filtered colimit. The module/abelian cohomology comparison, natural in every coefficient endomorphism, makes this an $A$-linear statement for the modules at hand. Consequently the colimit of the maps from Step 4 gives
$$H^q(X,M)\otimes_AB=\varinjlim_i(H^q(X,M)\otimes_AP_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}\varinjlim_iH^q(X,T(P_i))\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(X,T(B)).$$
The first identification is tensor preservation of the module colimit; the last is filtered cohomology continuity. On each colimit leg this is exactly $\alpha_{P_i}^q$, so the resulting map is the specified $\alpha_B^q$, regardless of the presentation.

source.place: Tag 073K, final displayed calculation and explanations; algebra Tag 058G; spaces-cohomology Tag 073E

proof.text: Compose $\alpha_B^q$, $H^q(\rho)$ from Step 3, and the affine cohomology comparison from Step 2. This gives an isomorphism $\gamma^q:H^q(X,M)\otimes_AB\to H^q(X',h^*M)$. At $a\otimes1$ the coefficient map is $m\mapsto\rho(m\otimes1)=\eta_h(m)$. The cohomology-fmap calculus is applied on the enlarged etale sites $\mathcal C_X,\mathcal C_{X'}$, which have terminal objects $X,X'$ and, by the site-model lemma, the same ringed topoi, module categories and direct images as the small sites (a small etale site of an algebraic space need not have a terminal object); the module/abelian comparison identifies its module cohomology with the abelian cohomology of the affine comparison. Thus the composite is the usual cohomological pullback: the cohomology-fmap calculus identifies the affine comparison with the map for the identity coefficient $h_*N\to h_*N$, and its composition with $M\xrightarrow{\eta_h}h_*N$ is the pullback for that unit. In general $\gamma^q(a\otimes b)=b\,h^*a$. This also proves naturality in $M$ and $B$ without making Lazard presentations functorial.

source.place: Tag 073K, affine calculation; sites-cohomology Tag 0736, augmentation/unit normalization

proof.text: The map $\gamma^q$ just proved invertible is the affine-sections map of the exchange in Step 1. Here is its normalization. Choose injective resolutions $M\to I$ and $h^*M\to J$ in nonnegative degrees. The flat ringed exchange resolution-unit equality says that on any bounded-below representative its composite with $g^*$ of the right-derived comparison unit is the ordinary termwise mate followed by the right-derived comparison unit on the target. Its adjoint is therefore induced by the coefficient unit $M\to h_*h^*M$; composing the ordinary mate with the unit gives precisely this unit, by the triangle identities. The cohomology-fmap calculus computes its action on global classes from such augmentation-preserving comparison maps, and identifies it with $a\mapsto h^*a$. Both the exchange map on affine sections and $\gamma^q$ are $B$-linear, so agreement on $a\otimes1$ proves agreement on $a\otimes b$ and their finite sums. As in Step 6 the calculus is applied on the enlarged sites, which have terminal objects. For the source and target sections we use the affine-base higher-image isomorphisms for $f$ and for $f'$, and affine tensor pullback; $f'$ is quasi-compact by base-change permanence of quasi-compactness and quasi-separated since its diagonal is a base change of that of $f$; higher images are quasi-coherent. Thus no arbitrary abstract cohomology isomorphism has been substituted for the canonical exchange.

source.place: Tag 073K, first paragraph reduction to clause (2); sites-cohomology Tag 0736 proof and Tag 07A7

proof.text: For arbitrary $Y,Y'$, choose affine etale charts $V\to Y$ and affine etale charts $V'\to Y'\times_YV$. Their composites cover $Y'$. The resulting map $V\prime\to V$ is flat: the base-changed $g$ is flat on scheme charts; etale chart ring maps are flat, and composites of flat ring maps are flat. Apply the affine flatness criterion on scheme charts. The quasi-compact affine-test statement makes $X_V$ quasi-compact; quasi-separatedness is preserved since its relative diagonal is the base change of the diagonal of $f$, and quasi-compact maps are stable under base change. With $V$ affine, the source is also absolutely quasi-separated as in Step 2. Higher-image etale restriction and canonical tensor-pullback composition identify the restriction of $\beta^q$ with the map for $X_V\to V$ and $V'\to V$. For the arrows, this follows from mate pasting applied to the two localization squares, whose comparisons are the canonical restrictions; the site model identifies those squares with actual localized etale ringed sites. Each restricted map is invertible: its source and target are quasi-coherent on the affine scheme $V'$ (higher images are quasi-coherent and tensor pullback preserves quasi-coherence), its map of global sections is the isomorphism $\gamma^q$ by Step 7, and by the affine-chart calculus a quasi-coherent module on $V'$ is the module associated to its global sections, functorially, so a map of such modules that is an isomorphism on global sections is an isomorphism. A sheaf morphism invertible on a covering is invertible: the local inverses agree on overlaps by uniqueness of inverses and glue by the sheaf axiom. This proves clause (1).

source.place: Tag 073K, reduction etale locally to affine bases; spaces-properties Tag 03LX; sites-cohomology Tag 0E47

proof.text:
For a second flat map $k:Y''\to Y'$, apply horizontal mate pasting to the derived pullback squares for $g$ and $k$. The pullback comparisons are the canonical derived composition comparisons, with their adjunction-compatible counits. The pasted inverse-image square is that for $gk$, since the fibre-product identifications preserve both projections. Hence the equality of mates is
$$\beta_{gk,M[0]}=\beta_{k,L(g')^*M[0]}\circ Lk^*(\beta_{g,M[0]})$$
under those comparisons. The base changes of $k$ are flat, so every horizontal pullback here is exact, by Step 1. Taking $H^q$ and the exact-functor cohomology identifications gives the required equality for $\beta^q$, with $(g')^*M$ as the coefficient of the second square. Naturality is already part of the mate construction and persists under cohomology. The affine formula and its value at $a\otimes1$ are Steps 6 and 7. All uses of finiteness in the argument were qcqs continuity or finite free stages; no hypothesis on $f$ other than qcqs has entered.
